coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Building 102 (former Power House)
record.summary: The 1912 Classical Revival powerhouse on 20th Street between Buildings 101 and 104, designed by Charles Peter Weeks, which generated compressed air and distributed electricity for the shipyard and still housed BAE Systems' electrical service when rehabilitation began. Orton rebuilt it as office space with a mezzanine and a rear addition (about 15,300-18,000 sq ft) and subleased it to JUUL Labs for ten years; the current occupant is unknown.

notes.accuracy_caveat: Real, surveyed building footprint -- high confidence in the outline itself. CORRECTED 2026-09-29: this footprint's area (~1955 m2 / ~21,043 sqft) does not match the building. The National Register nomination gives Building 102's dimensions as 128 ft 6 in by 42 ft 4 in (about 5,440 sqft, ~505 m2 as a rectangle), so this outline is roughly four times the building's own footprint and probably includes neighboring structures or other area; the '11,266 sf' Port figure is not the likely source of the discrepancy. The geometry has been accepted as is and was not changed; the outline should not be read as the building's own footprint.
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outline; not tied to an Assessor parcel).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: The former Assessor lot blklot 4046001 (which held Buildings 101, 102, 104 and 122/123 in the 2013 HPC packet) was retired on 2018-10-02 (DataSF Assessor parcels, active=false); in DataSF's current layer this footprint falls within active lot 3941041, which has no street address. No cited source ties the building to a current lot, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, extracted and matched individually.
notes.regulatory_context: The former Power House, built 1912, part of the same 20th Street Historic Core rehabilitation by Orton Development Inc. (ODI) as Building 101 (HPC packet 2013.1168E, Nov 26 2013 review). Per that packet, Building 102 was 'in fairly good condition' at the time and in use as the powerhouse facility. Port Item 12A (memo dated Jan 4, 2019) names JUUL Labs as the ten-year sublessee of the entire building less the Port's basement electrical equipment room, and Potrero View (Mar 2019) says JUUL 'sublets offices in Building 102'; no source after 2020 confirms a current occupant.

facts.value: Orton Development, Inc. through Historic Pier 70, LLC (66-year master lease L-15814 from the Port of San Francisco)
Marcy Wong Donn Logan Architects (design architect); Mark Hulbert, Preservation Architecture (historic architect)

Developer equity up to $14 million plus loans; Port participation rent of 50% of revenues above debt and a 14% equity return; sources in 2018: Port capital $1.8M, Seismic Safety Loan $23.6M, historic tax credit equity $20.4M, private debt and equity $81.2M
Contributing resource to the Union Iron Works Historic District (NRHP, listed April 17, 2014)
Tall rectangular concrete building with hipped mission-tile roof, five arched bays, terra cotta shell frieze and copper cornice
128 ft 6 in by 42 ft 4 in by 48 ft tall
8,428 (NRHP, first floor and basement); 11,266 before and 15,331 after rehabilitation (Port 2019 Table 1); 15,500 original and just over 18,000 after per Retrofit magazine
Office (subleased to JUUL Labs, 10-year term, entire building less the Port's basement electrical room)
JUUL Labs subleased Building 102 (and 104); the presence of an e-cigarette maker on Port land drew public objection in 2018-2019
Powerhouse No. 1 Electric: offices, four air compressors, three rotary converters, switchboard and transformers on the main floor; still serving some of BAE Systems' electrical needs in 2013
'Building 102 key historic features' listed by the Port as publicly accessible

open_questions: Current tenant: JUUL's sublease was to run ten years from completion (2019), but no source after 2020 confirms JUUL is still in Building 102 or names a successor.
Completion / certificate of occupancy date: the Port anticipated 2019; the November 2020 profile describes the finished building without a date.
The square-footage figures disagree by source (8,428 NRHP floor area vs 11,266 Port pre-rehab vs 15,500 magazine); the NRHP figure may exclude the basement.
